hypothesis: Fresh completed-five-minute ETH breakout onsets filtered by prior one-minute BBWP compression and a directional pullback may retain a small repeatable edge after live taker friction with a 60-bps protective stop and 12-hour maximum hold.
decision: Retain the exact 12-hour ETH exit contract and reject global four-hour, eight-hour, and tested early-profit-lock replacements. The resolved live short surrendered most of a 50.46-bps favorable excursion and closed slightly negative after costs, but that single path does not overturn the fixed-entry duration evidence: four hours failed the 282-trade development partition, eight hours failed the 56-trade opened-final partition, and twelve hours was the only duration positive in both. Continue exact long/short and breakout-relation attribution and test any future exit mechanism prospectively without changing entry authority, route, size, stop, or live runtime under this revision.
falsifier: The duration decision is invalidated by failure to reproduce the exact 282-development and 56-opened-final fixed-entry cohorts, changed stop or cost assumptions, side or timestamp drift, or execution authority. Revisit the 12-hour hold if a preregistered shorter or state-aware exit improves after-cost net return in both historical partitions and later independent live long and short lifecycles without largest-winner dependence.
limitations: The entry policy and 60-bps/12-hour control were selected after prior historical trials.
The opened-final 60-day partition was previously inspected and is descriptive rather than sealed evidence.
The twelve-hour opened-final result becomes negative after removing its largest winner, so it is retained as the least contradicted tested duration rather than a proven optimum.
Long and short leadership still rotates between chronological partitions.
Completed one-minute bars cannot reproduce intrabar stop ordering, private IOC latency, hidden liquidity, or exact counterfactual fills.
